newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil ignores stock draw.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil ignores stock draw.

text.p: Singapore front month gas oil swaps was down late afternoon on Thursday despite a large drawdown in middle distillate stocks as the market was still weighed down by the prompt physical overhang, traders said.
"July gas oil is weak despite the stock draw because people think there is still alot of unsold cargoes around," a trader said.
July swaps were indicated at $22.25/$22.35 per barrel, down 15 cents from Wednesday while August was quoted unchanged at $22.85/$22.95, brokers said.
August traded earlier in the day at $22.90, they said.

Singapore's weekly middle distillate stocks were down for the first time since end May, falling by 1.331 million barrels to 10.744 million in the week ending July 2, Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) data showed on Thursday.
But traders said at 10.744 million the stocks are still high compared to the normal levels of around 6 million barrels.
Concerns over unsold physical barrels continued to dominate the market and some players think more players will emerge to sell as the market moves forward to trade second half July barrels.
On Wednesday, a European major sold to a Chinese trader 30,000 tonne for July 17-21 lifting at $163 per tonne or around $21.90 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
Signs of excess prompt were clearly seen in the recent floating deals where cargoes were done at about 60 cents and 75 cents below spot Singapore quotes on a fob basis.
Worries of the overhang is extending to the further out months which are also heavily in contango with July/August valued at minus 65 cents and trades seen for Aug/Sep at minus 65 cents as well.
The jet fuel swaps were steady with July regrade last quoted at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil is also unchanged with July swaps quoted at $98.75/$99.25 per tonne.

Naphtha swaps firmed because of the recent crude rally and possible production cut in Japan due to the oil spill in Tokyo Bay. August swaps were last quoted at $20.90/$21.10, up from Wednesday's $20.70/$20.90, brokers said.
August traded late on Wednesday at $20.90, $20.95. $20.80, and $20.85, they said.
